# whoami — Full Documentation

> whoami is a persistent AI identity profile service that syncs your personal context across all AI agents — including Cursor, Claude, Codex, Windsurf and Cline. One profile, every AI. Free and open source.

## What is whoami?

whoami gives every AI agent a persistent identity profile about you. Instead of repeating yourself every time you start a new conversation, you write your profile once and every AI reads the same you.

### The Problems whoami Solves

1. **Switch AI, Lose Identity**: You move from Codex to Claude, and it has no idea who you are. You start over. Again.
2. **New Chat, Blank Slate**: Even with the same AI, every new conversation starts from zero. Your context, preferences, history — all gone.
3. **Can't Edit What AI Knows**: You want to update how AI sees you, but the settings are buried or locked. There's no easy way to manage your AI identity.

whoami solves all three. One profile, synced everywhere, fully in your control.

## Getting Started

### Option A: Tell Your AI Agent (Easiest)

Paste this prompt to any AI agent (Cursor, Claude, Codex, etc.):

```
Install a cross-AI agent user identity sync skill by running: npx skills add MorvanZhou/whoami. After installation, open https://whoamiagent.com/login?redirect=dashboard to register or login to get an API key.
```

Your AI will handle the rest — installation, login, and configuration.

### Option B: Install Manually

```bash
npx skills add MorvanZhou/whoami
```

Then visit [whoamiagent.com](https://whoamiagent.com) to sign in with GitHub or Google and get your API key.

## How It Works

```
You ──→ Install whoami skill on your AI agent
         │
         ├─ Sign in at whoamiagent.com → Get API key
         │
         ├─ Dashboard gives a one-time URL → AI downloads config automatically
         │
         ├─ AI agent fetches your profile at conversation start
         │
         └─ You share new info → AI saves it → All AIs know it
```

1. **Install** — Add the whoami skill to your AI agent via `npx skills add MorvanZhou/whoami`
2. **Sign in** — Create an account at [whoamiagent.com](https://whoamiagent.com) and grab an API key
3. **Configure** — The dashboard provides a one-time URL for secure API key delivery. Your AI agent downloads it and saves the config automatically — no need to copy-paste keys manually
4. **Talk** — Start any conversation. Your AI automatically loads your profile and knows who you are
5. **Update** — Mention something new about yourself. Your AI saves it, and every AI agent you use learns it

## Core Features

### Cross-AI Identity Sync
Write your profile once on whoami — Claude, Codex, Cursor, and every AI agent reads the same you. No more re-introducing yourself when switching between AI tools.

### Persistent Context
Your profile lives in the cloud. New chat, new day — every session starts with full context. Your identity never disappears between conversations.

### User-Controlled Profile
Update your profile from the dashboard or just tell your AI. Changes sync to all agents instantly. You own your identity — edit, update, or delete anytime.

### Agent Skill Architecture
whoami works as an AI agent skill — a standardized extension that any compatible AI agent can install and use. Install once, works everywhere.

### Free & Open Source
Completely free to use. No cost, no lock-in. MIT licensed. Sign up with GitHub or Google and start immediately.

## What Gets Saved in Your Profile?

Your profile is a simple Markdown document (up to 5000 characters). It can include anything you want your AIs to know:

- Your name and role
- Technical skills and experience
- Communication preferences
- Project context and workflows
- Coding style preferences
- Favorite tools and frameworks
- Anything that helps AI assist you better

You have full control — edit, update, or delete your profile anytime from the [dashboard](https://whoamiagent.com/dashboard).

## Supported Platforms

whoami works with any AI agent that supports the skill protocol, including:

| Platform | Status |
|----------|--------|
| Cursor | ✅ Supported |
| Claude Code | ✅ Supported |
| OpenAI Codex | ✅ Supported |
| Windsurf | ✅ Supported |
| Cline | ✅ Supported |
| OpenClaw | ✅ Supported |
| Any skill-compatible agent | ✅ Supported |

## Usage Examples

### Example 1: Auto-load at Conversation Start

**User says**: "Help me write a Python script to process CSV"

**Agent behavior**:
1. Fetches user profile via whoami skill
2. Learns user preferences (e.g., "prefers concise code style", "uses pandas")
3. Generates code matching the user's style and preferences

### Example 2: User Saves Info Proactively

**User says**: "Remember that I'm a backend developer skilled in Go and Rust"

**Agent behavior**:
1. Fetches existing profile
2. Merges new info into existing profile
3. Updates remote profile via whoami skill
4. Confirms save success — all other AI agents now have the updated info

### Example 3: First-Time Setup

**User says**: "Do you know me?"

**Agent behavior**:
1. Checks for whoami configuration
2. If not configured, opens browser login page and guides setup
3. If already configured, displays profile summary and continues the task

## Security & Privacy

- **API Key Security**: API keys are never stored in plaintext in the database — only SHA256 hashes
- **OAuth Authentication**: Sign in securely with GitHub or Google — no passwords stored
- **CSRF Protection**: OAuth state parameters protect against cross-site request forgery
- **JWT Cookies**: Authentication uses HttpOnly JWT cookies with 7-day expiration
- **CORS Policy**: Only whoamiagent.com is allowed
- **User Control**: You can delete your profile and data at any time

For full details, see our [Privacy Policy](https://whoamiagent.com/privacy).

## Technical Details

- **Config file path**: `~/.whoamiagent` (cross-platform: macOS/Linux/Windows)
- **Profile format**: Markdown
- **Profile max length**: 5000 characters
- **History versions**: Last 3 versions retained automatically
- **Script dependencies**: Python standard library only (zero third-party dependencies)
- **API prefix**: All endpoints under `/api/`
